transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14
Time: 15:00 - 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Alex Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CTO, ApexHealth), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Security)

Summary: weekly pilot sync for Redwood Private (VPC) pilot. Focus: network peering, routing fallback, recent perf runs, and upcoming runtime upgrade.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh happy wednesday. quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya: maya here, maya singh.
[00:10] Liam: liam on our infra team.
[00:12] Priya: priya from security.
[00:14] Samir: great, alex?
[00:15] Alex: alex chen from redwood, se on the pilot. quick agenda - run through the perf results from last week, network status, the patch/upgrade plan, then security questions. sound good?
[00:24] Maya: yep, go for it.

[00:30] Alex: ok so first the perf spreadsheet - i ran the 2k token baseline again and then did a 3k burst test. numbers we saw: p99 latency 280ms for 2k baseline, and the 3k burst pushed p99 to ~430ms. cpu utilization for the host was stable ~65%, gpu util 78-86 during the run. i also captured kv cache hit rates - we were seeing ~18% prefix cache hits due to variability in prompt distribution.
[00:55] Liam: hmm 18% seems low, we thought caching would help more for the assistant-templates. are you using the same prefix keys we gave?
[01:02] Alex: yeah i'm using the keys; there may be some tokenization differences - our runtime canonicalizes whitespace differently, so it split some tokens. i'll add a note in the sheet.
[01:10] Maya: could that explain the p99 bump in the 3k run?
[01:13] Alex: partly, and also the scheduler at that time consolidated smaller requests into the same batch which increased sequence length of some batches - we need a more aggressive knob to cap batching for low latency flows.

[01:28] Samir: about the knob - we have an autoscale/batching policy we can tune. alex, can you outline what we'd change?
[01:35] Alex: sure - there are two quick levers: max batch size and latency cap. for low-latency routes we set max batch size to 4 and a latency cap of 150ms; for throughput routes we push batch size to 16. for your use case (interactive clinical assistant) we recommend low-latency profile with forced small batches and prefix cache priming. also we can enable per-route eviction for KV to bump hit rates.
[02:00] Liam: ok that makes sense. please push the new policy to the pilot cluster and we'll observe. can you do that before the 4k run?
[02:07] Alex: yes i'll push a policy today in staging and then to pilot tomorrow morning.

[02:14] Priya: on networking, last week we saw packet drops on the VPC peering from your control-plane egress IPs. did you guys identify cause?
[02:23] Samir: we dug into the egress IP list - turns out there was a mismatch in the expected CIDR you gave vs what our control plane was actual sending from. alex, remind them what we need.
[02:33] Alex: we need inbound firewall rules to allow 10.1.2.0/24 and 52.18.190.12/32 (control plane) and 52.18.190.13/32 (fallback). earlier the peering route table had a more restrictive mask and some routes were blackholed which caused intermittent TCP resets.
[02:52] Liam: yeah i see in our VPC logs some RSTs around 03:42 UTC that line up with the test runs. i'll open the rule change and push by monday EOD.
[02:59] Priya: will that be enough for security? we need to make sure traffic is encrypted end-to-end and keys are never in plaintext on nodes.
[03:07] Alex: yes encryption in transit is TLS 1.3; for KMS we integrate with your KMS via external key references, so nodes never store raw keys. for the on-prem packaging we mount a hardware-backed keystore if you provide an HSM.
[03:22] Priya: do you have docs we can review?
[03:24] Samir: we'll send the security packet after this call, includes KMS integration doc, SOC2 artifacts pointer, and our SSO/SAML guide.

[03:33] Maya: quick question on the upgrade - you mentioned patch 1.2.0 with a new kernel selection and attention optimization. what risks should we expect?
[03:43] Alex: the 1.2.0 patch includes a new fused attention kernel plus a change to the kv cache layout. benefits are reduced per-token latency and lower memory overhead. risks: the kv layout change is backward-incompatible for old checkpoints, so we recommend a rolling deploy with canary and a fallback image. we tested the fallback path but we want to run your model in canary before full rollout.
[04:05] Liam: how long does the rollout take? our maintenance windows are tight.
[04:09] Alex: the canary can be scheduled for a 30-60 minute window; full rollout depends on number of pods - for your pilot cluster it's about 2 hours total including validation. we'll provide a runbook with exact steps.

[04:24] Maya: awesome. on the benchmarking - we want a 4k token workload to simulate long patient summaries. can you confirm memory footprint and expected latency?
[04:34] Alex: early estimate with the new kernel is p95 ~650ms for 4k tokens on the pilot node type; memory peak ~62GB per model instance. running now on our infra it came in at ~600-720ms depending on batch mixing. we'll do the formal 4k run and attach full traces.
[04:51] Priya: please include stack traces and any unexpected OOMs. we need to see failure modes.
[04:55] Alex: will do.

[05:00] Samir: any other blockers?
[05:02] Liam: firewall rule and then i'd like the control-plane IP list in a single file we can ingest to our ipset.
[05:10] Samir: i'll send that post-call.

[05:14] Maya: on pricing, did we get the committed nodes pricing?
[05:18] Samir: yes alex will follow up with a pricing addendum for the Dedicated-style commit for pilot if you want reserved capacity later; for Private there's a different billing construct, i'll include both scenarios in a short appendix.
[05:30] Alex: action items and deliverables - i'll run the 4k perf test, attach logs and the tracing output to the sheet. samir will post the upgrade runbook and checksums. we'll also hand over the installer window options.
[05:45] Priya: one more on compliance — can you confirm retention of logs for audit? we need 365-day retention for some artifact types.
[05:54] Samir: default retention is 90 days for debug traces, but we can enable longer retention as an add-on - i'll include retention tiers in the security packet.
[06:05] Maya: ok great, that covers it. thanks everyone.
[06:08] Samir: thanks, we'll follow up on the items. meeting closed.
notes: Alex to push new batching policy to pilot cluster
Samir to send control-plane IP list and upgrade runbook
Priya to circulate compliance checklist responses
